summary: Cuilan Liu works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology. Liu held positions as Assistant Professor of Buddhist Studies at Emmanuel College, Toronto (attested 2017) and at the University of Munich (attested 2018).

Culadasa (1944–2021) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar and teacher who studied under the traditional teacher Joti Dhamma Bhikkhu. He served as director of Dharma Treasure Buddhist Sangha (attested 2011) and taught Matthew Immergut.
Cuma Ozkan specializes in religious studies and Sinology. Ozkan earned a Master of Arts at the University of Iowa under MA supervisor Morten Schlütter (attested 2013).
Cunda studied under Ajahn Pasanno and Ajahn Amaro.

Cuong T. Mai specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He earned an MA from the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and a PhD from Indiana University Bloomington under John R. McRae, later serving as Adjunct Lecturer at the University of Vermont.

Cynthea J. Bogel works in Japanology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Bogel completed doctoral studies under John M. Rosenfield and held a post at the University of Washington (attested 2004–2009).
Cynthia Col specializes in Sinology and religious studies. She studied Chinese religion at the Graduate Theological Union (attested 2003) and was taught by Mark Elliott and Steven D. Goodman.

Cynthia M. Beall (born 1949) specializes in Tibetology. She earned a B.A. from the University of Pennsylvania and an M.A. from Pennsylvania State University before joining Case Western Reserve University in 1976 as Distinguished University Professor and S. Idell Pyle Professor of Anthropology.

Cynthia Talbot (born 1952) specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and became Professor emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2026).

Cyril Alexander Rylands was an Indologist and linguist who earned a B.A. and M.A. from the University of Cambridge. He served as Lecturer in Sanskrit at SOAS University of London until 1961, teaching Thomas Welbourne Clark and Ludo Rocher.

Cyril Henry Philips (1912–2005) was a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Liverpool and SOAS (Ph.D.). He served as Director of SOAS (1946–1980), succeeding Ralph Lilley Turner in 1955, and was Vice-Chancellor of the University of London (1972–1976).
Cyril Walter Gurner (1888–1969) was an Indology scholar who earned M.A. degrees from Oriel College and the University of London. He served as Treasurer at The Asiatic Society (attested 1944).

Cyrill von Korvin-Krasinski (1905–1992) worked in Tibetology and religious studies. He completed a Ph.D. at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz by 1948 and served as director of the school at Maria Laach Abbey.

Cyrus Ransom Pangborn (1916–1989) worked in religious studies and Indology, studying at Kansas Wesleyan, Yale, and Columbia. He taught religion at the University of Iowa (1951–1954) and was Associate Professor of Religion at Rutgers University (1954–1982).

Cyrus Stearns specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Washington under Leonard van der Kuijp, also studying under Turrell V. Wylie and several traditional teachers, and worked as a translator for the Tsadra Foundation.
Cândido de Figueiredo (1846–1925) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied law at the University of Coimbra (1869–1874) and served as a teacher at Liceu Central beginning in 1882.
Cécile Ducher specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD under Matthew T. Kapstein at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, where she later served as a research fellow.

Célestin Bouglé (1870–1940) was a philosopher and Indologist who studied at École Normale Supérieure. He held posts at the universities of Montpellier, Toulouse, and Paris, became Professor at the Sorbonne (1909), and served as Director of the ENS (1935–1940).

D. C. Lau (1921–2010) was a scholar of Sinology and philosophy who studied at the University of Hong Kong and University of Glasgow. He held professorships at the University of London and The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
D. C. Sarasvati studied Indology under V. Raghavan and served as a Lecturer-cum-Research Assistant at the University of Madras from 1964 to 1965.
